packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-05 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

EXPOSURE STATEMENT
No proposed identification or earlier reading of this item was present in my
context. I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001..010 in this packet; no packet.json,
no web, no search. Nothing beyond the rules.

1. LAYOUT SURVEY (image only)

Two overviews (image-001, image-006), each a tall narrow crop of a book gutter,
upright. They appear to show the two faces of one narrow vertical parchment strip
bound into the gutter of a host book, photographed through or beside thin,
translucent host leaves.

The strip:
- Darker (tan) parchment, about 4-6 letters wide, the full height of the crop.
- A formal upright book hand in black ink, noticeably larger and heavier than the
  host writing; horizontal ruling visible between lines.
- About 24 lines on the image-001 face and about 25 on the image-006 face. Every
  line is cut at both sides, so no complete word is guaranteed anywhere.
- Coloured one-line initials: image-001 face has a blue (pale blue-green) initial
  about two thirds down and a red initial near the foot; image-006 face has a
  red initial at mid-height and a blue one near the foot. Each is cut by the
  strip edge and looks like a round letter (O, D or Q). Observation: alternating
  red and blue small initials at short intervals. Tentative interpretation:
  text divided into short units (verses or short sentences). Punctuation ":"
  occurs within lines several times. I infer no work.
- On image-001 the right edge of the strip is overlapped by a translucent host
  leaf, so the last letter or two of each strip line there is seen through that
  leaf and mixed with its cursive writing.

The host leaves (not the strip):
- Pale, thin leaves with a rapid cursive hand in grey-black ink. To the right of
  the strip: line-openings of about 24 lines, the first beginning with a large
  cursive capital with a long descending stroke; another larger capital with a
  long stroke about two thirds down (paragraph openings, tentatively).
- To the left of the strip: only final strokes and flourishes of line-ends from
  another page, plus a tiny two-line note in very pale ink in the margin
  (image-002, left of the strip).
- Much of the cursive is doubled by show-through.
No running titles, rubrics or glosses are visible in these crops; they are too
narrow to show page layout or column count.

2. SPANS SELECTED
The strip is the only element with enough ink to transcribe, so I read every
line of both faces from the tiles (002-005 and 007-010). The host cursive was
examined and only its line-openings are listed, as tentative. Unread: everything
outside the crop. Which strip face is recto or verso, and whether the strip
stands the right way up relative to its original leaf, cannot be settled from
the images (the letters are upright as mounted).

Conventions: "..." before or after = line cut by the strip edge; "?" after an
uncertain reading; alternatives separated by "/"; abbreviation marks kept
(tilde = stroke above); expansions in parentheses. Line numbers count strip
lines from the top of the named tile. Tiles overlap by one to three lines; the
overlaps are marked and are not additional text. Because every group is a
mid-line fragment of four to six letters, minims (i, n, m, u) cannot be divided
securely and I have NOT resolved them from sense.

3. TRANSCRIPTION - THE STRIP

--- Face 1: image-001 (overview) ---

image-002 l.1   ...ime? / ...une?
image-002 l.2   ...ituu? ...        (a, t, then four minims: "atuu"/"ituu")
image-002 l.3   ...assa. ...        (or "alla."; a point follows)
image-002 l.4   ...ctur? / ...etur?
image-002 l.5   ...eiũ? ...         (minims with a stroke above; "ciũ"/"eiũ")
image-002 l.6   ...tra? / ...ura?
image-002 l.7   ...is e...          (or "9 e..." with the -us sign)

image-003 l.1-2 = image-002 l.6-7 (overlap)
image-003 l.3   ...tessi? / ...testi? ...   (tall double letter, ss or st)
image-003 l.4   ...enti? / ...erui? ...
image-003 l.5   ...ũ ee? ...        (stroke over u; then "ee"/"eð" with mark: esse?)
image-003 l.6   ...atur? / ...atus?
image-003 l.7   ...t ab...
image-003 l.8   ...mini? ...        (six or seven minims; "nuni"/"mini"/"muu")
image-003 l.9   ...s fili? / ...s fui? ...

image-004 l.1-2 = image-003 l.8-9 (overlap)
image-004 l.3   ...rita? ...
image-004 l.4   ...s ie? / ...sice? ...
image-004 l.5   ...do ill...
image-004 l.6   ...debi? / ...dehi? ...
image-004 l.7   ...trã? ...         (stroke above the a; a further letter cut)
image-004 l.8   ...t? [BLUE initial, round: O/D/Q?] ...
image-004 l.9   ...lebo? / ...debo? ...
image-004 l.10  ...: au? ...        (tops only here; = image-005 l.2)

image-005 l.1-2 = image-004 l.9-10 (overlap); l.2 reads  ...s?: au? / ...: ati? ...
image-005 l.3   ...nitur? / ...mtus? ...
image-005 l.4   ...ama? / ...anna? ...   (stroke above; minims between two a's)
image-005 l.5   ... . in? / ... : iu? ...
image-005 l.6   ...e [RED initial, round, cut: O/D/Q?] ...
image-005 l.7   ...erib? / ...enli? ...
image-005 l.8   ...ali? / ...ill? ...    (foot of strip, stained)

--- Face 2: image-006 (overview) ---

image-007 l.1   ...nter? / ...ater? ...
image-007 l.2   ...ibus? / ...ilua? ...   (a small mark above the first letters)
image-007 l.3   ...nea...
image-007 l.4   ...s? hb? ...       (a tall letter then "hb" with stroke: h(a)b...?)
image-007 l.5   ...ti in? / ...u in...    (stroke above "in")
image-007 l.6   ...a su? / ...asu...      (or "a sũ")
image-007 l.7   ...ehs? / ...elis? / ...eius? ...

image-008 l.1-2 = image-007 l.6-7 (overlap)
image-008 l.3   ...iceri? / ...icem? ...
image-008 l.4   ...a atq...         (probably "atq(ue)", the q cut)
image-008 l.5   ...ipie? / ...cipie...
image-008 l.6   ...[two or three faint brownish strokes, possibly an erased or
                 cancelled letter group] fec? / fer? ...
image-008 l.7   ...recor? / ...tecu? ...
image-008 l.8   ...n tu...
image-008 l.9   ...ti? tr? [RED initial, round, cut: O/D?] ...

image-009 l.1-2 = image-008 l.8-9 (overlap)
image-009 l.3   ...filios...        (the clearest group on the strip; initial f
                                     partly lost, "[f]ilios" or "[a]lios")
image-009 l.4   ...cuitu? / ...eiuitu? ...   (c/e then eight or nine minims and t)
image-009 l.5   ...simia? / ...sinna? ...    (tall s or f, then minims)
image-009 l.6   ...a: in? / ...a: Tu? ...    (colon-like punctuation after a)
image-009 l.7   ...atq(ue)? eu...
image-009 l.8   ...t? pau...        (or "o pau")
image-009 l.9   ...illos...

image-010 l.1   = image-009 l.9 (overlap)  ...illos...
image-010 l.2   ...as? ⁊? u? ...     (blurred; "aed"/"as⁊ u")
image-010 l.3   ...s [BLUE initial, round with a vertical bar or reserve: O/D/Q?] ...
image-010 l.4   ...ahu? / ...abit? ...
image-010 l.5   ...ome? / ...anne? ...
image-010 l.6   ...cup? / ...aup? ...   (stroke above; descender on last letter, p)
image-010 l.7   ...bus? / ...bius? ...
image-010 l.8   ...ul? / ...til? ...    (foot of strip, damaged)

4. HOST LEAVES (not the strip) - line-openings only, all tentative

Cursive to the right of the strip, best seen on image-006 and tiles 007-010
(the same writing appears on image-001, tiles 002-005, partly under the strip
edge; that is the same text, not more text):
  large cursive capital (P? with long descender) followed by signs like "33" /
  "ulteri?" / "Cupim?" / "nõ m..." / "ad m..." / "⁊ dei?" / "aie d..." /
  "cuy?" / "Inimic?" / "nõ vu..." / "de aq..." / "Cetera?" / "q' al.. I..." /
  "Boni?" / "Et d..." / "q(uo)d?" / larger capital then "ed" (Sed?) /
  "dei g..." / "ad m..." / "domic?" / "S..." / "Sic p?" / "S..." / "Dette?" /
  "Primo?"
These are 3-6 letters each, blurred and doubled by show-through; I would not
match on them.

Left of the strip: only terminal flourishes and endings ("...it", "...ua",
"...ie", "...g"); nothing transcribable. The small pale marginal note on
image-002 has two lines, perhaps "Sol?" / "fuit?" - [illegible] in practice.

5. LIMITATIONS
- The strip preserves a vertical slice only. With four to six letters per line
  and no line complete, there is no connected prose to give; the transcription
  is a column of letter groups. The securest groups are: "...assa." (or
  "alla."), "...is e", "...t ab", "...do ill", "...nea", "...a atq", "...n tu",
  "...filios", "...illos", and the ":" punctuation at image-005 l.2 and
  image-009 l.6. A match would have to be tested as a vertical sequence at a
  fixed column offset, for example (face 2) nea / ... / a atq / ..ipie.. /
  ..fec.. / ..rec.. / n tu / [red initial] / filios / ... / a: .. / atq eu? /
  pau / illos.
- Minim groups are unresolved; several "?" alternatives differ only in how the
  minims are divided.
- On image-001 the right edge of the strip is under a translucent host leaf,
  which adds cursive strokes over the last letters of each line.
- Focus is soft in all tiles (slight blur, glare from a transparent sheet).
- Needed: an image of the strip freed from the overlapping leaf, in sharper
  focus; if the strip continues into the fold, the hidden width would add the
  letters most needed.
- This is an unverified image reading.
